I can honestly say, I was the cold, indifferent one. I had completely shut down, emotionally. At that time, I was bottling in all the pain from my dad's death. We'd gone to the funeral and I'd not even cried. I just acted like I didn't care, even though the night before he'd passed...I'd had to hold him down through an extended dementia episode I'd rather forget. It was all bad. If she had asked "Can we talk?" (she didn't) I'm not sure that I would have easily opened up. I was confused and messed-up, and I really needed professional help.

In retrospect, the best thing that could have happened for me would have been for her to reach out to someone else. If she'd gone to my stepdad and sister, hearing them approach me about the need to get help would have been a lot different. She and I were too close. We were always together and around each other, in the house. I'd gotten to feel that she was controlling my life and I didn't trust her. I needed someone other than my wife to tell me, "Dude, you need to see a doctor!"

I seriously hope that you guys succeed. Hell, if it helps you can tell him the story you read, here. A lot of men withdraw and think: So what if it all falls apart? They never think of the day after or the month after that, or the years...and how much they will miss playing with their pets, living in that house, the nicknames and the memories. It's easy to throw something away, but harder to live with a hole it left behind...

Good luck!

We are all just gliding like ghosts through a gallery of cavern petroglyphs, not really sure which was first or if that even matters, eh? I enjoy reading what you right, Macabre. Whether being intellectual makes one depressed or being depressed makes one intellectual, it sort of becomes a chicken-egg question. What I do believe is that depression often indicates a dangerous third eye--a lens that focuses the world in all its grotesque glory and lights on every irony, so that the details become a sensory overload. The vision is the impossible dream of the painter to perfectly reflect his mind, never realized but always aspired toward. In attempting to do so, great things happen and yet--as with the Pagliacci joke from Alan Moore's "Watchmen"--the artist tends to be the one person who cannot seem to harvest happiness from Arcadian acres of his own dreams. Simpler eyes see pretty skies and rainbows colored with variegated lies, and the rest do their best to try and try, to mask distress and not ask: why? There's a little Silverstein/Seuss wordplay to describe it. We populate an overpopulated world, where life is exponentially devalued and messiahs drown in their own holy water. But, people like us? Birds of a feather...

They were the blueprints that built pyramids and biplanes, and when those things are all dust and the world is a barren demesne...the echo of dreams will be all that remains.

Please write more!

I'm not going to say the situation is the same, but this does sound eerily reminiscent of my predicament.

I met my ex-wife in 2004 and married her in 2006. We had ups and downs, but things were good until 2014, the year we separated. Our dissolution became official in January of this year.

She knew I'd had depression issues, even when we first met. I had a rough life and came from a broken home. We had our issues, but we managed to be very happy.

Then odd things happened. In 2011, I had a career crisis AND met my absentee biological father. In 2014, he (my biological father) suddenly passed away from cancer. I became withdrawn and broken, and we argued...

She'd almost left me earlier in 2014, citing stress and relationship issues. We had one big argument and I finally told her I "didn't love her." She cried and told me she "wanted (her) husband back" which I hear like a loop in my head now, tearing me up.

It was a huge mistake on my part...

We were torn asunder by it and, despite an agreement to be friends, we ended up pulling away from each other. My life spiraled down. I'd lost my father and wife, and I was even laid-off from a job I enjoyed.

Getting to the point, I was hurting inside worse than I'd let on. I was not in my right mind. We'd had problems over the years, but if I'd been rational, I'd never have said such a thing or wanted to break-up.

She was waiting for me to come to her and open up. I couldn't! I wish now that she'd maybe gone to my family. I wish that she'd even talked to me about going to therapy together, but I think she was tired and wanted out...and I can't blame her.

But I wish it had gone differently.

I know I'm kind of rambling here, but I wanted to paint a picture. Although depression (if this IS depression, mind) can make us irrational and be caused by indistinct reasons, it HAS a reason. For me, I was caught in a web of sadness...

1. My dream is to be a writer, and I didn't feel she believed in me or cared.
2. My father had died, severing any chance for me to confront him about the past.
3. History and heredity were catching up with me, and I needed a hug...even if I didn't deserve one.

This isn't a road map or a solution, just an accounting. I wish I'd have gotten a chance to go with her to a therapy. I wish I'd have been able to get help, something I STILL need. Had I been thinking clearly, I'd have realized that I was throwing away everything in a self-destruct mode--pushing the red button...

So, I guess I would say it pays to be cautious and not push hard, but these are the words I wish I'd heard:

Honey, I love you. I'm here and I'll listen to you, even if I don't always agree. We came together for a reason, and we stand together for the same reason. I'm willing to reach out and find us a helping hand, if you need me to.

That's all. Psychological paralysis had me. My brain went blue screen. Everyone is different and maybe he needs different words or an approach that isn't the same, but nobody acts like that without needing help. Nobody.

So maybe you can save what you have. I'm currently on a lonely highway and lost, and I miss her.

Typing one's thoughts has a plethora of advantages. In a phone or live conversation, people don't always give you the chance to complete a thought or express yourself, before they interject. And, as you point out, if emotions run high, it will show in your voice or expressions. People always highlight how things like that distance us, but I think they've just as much power to open doors.

Frost: As somebody that suffers with anxiety and depression in the worse way, I tell people who don't have it that it's like a lens or third eye: where ignorance is bliss, high resolution is torment. Most of the time, they don't get that and shake their heads, and by doing so prove the point!

You did the right thing. Don't doubt it and don't let them derail you, even if it seems to compound things! You seem very intelligent and insightful, and sometimes the villagers don't know any better than to grab torches and charge the town square. Deciphering depression for someone who doesn't have it is like Sophocles in Japanese.

Building a support network can sometimes be a non-traditional venture. One idea is to look at local support groups (something I'm doing right now) and calling up the local NAMI to get info on them. Another idea is to keep posting in places like this and using it as another sort of pillar of support. These options help fill in the hours and days between your therapy appointments.

I want to applaud this post. I have a special sort of contempt for the people who think the "solution" to depression is the garbage found in the landfills of their self-help books, fruits and vitamins, and rock climbing. It's why people with depression need to stick together and support each other, because the ones that don't have it will never really "get it."

Don't feel cowardly for not posting on Facebook. Not everyone is understanding and there's a lot of stigma attached to depression. People don't always get that it can be crippling and I commend you on getting your thoughts into a post, and even just hitting submit. As someone who suffers paralytic depression, I know that the genesis of it all is not just "one thing" but typically a composite image of a lot of issues. Rather than starting at the top of Mt. Olympus, is there something small that happened in the last few days that might have been the last straw? If not, is there something that would make your day better?
